facts.raw_span: progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws
symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
intact, bluish-gray oral mucosa
no lymphadenopathy
routine hematologic tests were unremarkable
well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas involving the mandibular bodies, angles, ascending rami, and the maxillary tuberosities
bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of the cortical plates of the maxilla and mandible
mild anterior displacement of an unerupted first molar
no cortical breaches or soft-tissue extension
Vital signs were normal

concepts.why: The symmetrical, bilateral, and painless nature of the jaw swelling, along with the radiographic findings of well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas and expansile lesions, are characteristic of Cherubism.

concepts.why: The radiographic findings of well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas and expansile lesions, along with the displacement of the unerupted first molar, are consistent with Central Giant Cell Granuloma, although the absence of cortical breaches or soft-tissue extension is less typical.

support_spans: well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas involving the mandibular bodies, angles, ascending rami, and the maxillary tuberosities
bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of the cortical plates of the maxilla and mandible
concepts.why: The radiographic findings of well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas and expansile lesions are consistent with Fibrous Dysplasia, although the intact oral mucosa is less typical, as Fibrous Dysplasia often presents with mucosal changes.

rationales.F01: Bilateral jaw swelling is a key feature of Cherubism and Central Giant Cell Granuloma.
rationales.F02: Symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla is characteristic of Cherubism.
rationales.F06: Well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas are typical of Cherubism and Central Giant Cell Granuloma.
rationales.F07: Bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of the cortical plates are highly suggestive of Cherubism and Central Giant Cell Granuloma.
rationales.F09: The absence of cortical breaches or soft-tissue extension makes Fibrous Dysplasia less likely.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws and symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla specifically supports Cherubism.
